facts.claim: In Manual (default) mode reads inside the working directory run without asking while Bash commands (except a read-only built-in set), file edits, WebFetch and WebSearch ask for approval.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: permissions.defaultMode accepts default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, manual (alias of default); 'auto' and 'bypassPermissions' do not take effect from project or local settings (since v2.1.257 for bypass).
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: permissions.deny rules block in every mode including bypassPermissions; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode='disable' makes Claude Code reject --dangerously-skip-permissions.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Built-in starting permission mode: interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto on v2.1.283+; claude -p / Agent SDK start in default when the session fetches feature flags, and in auto (v2.1.285+) when it does not (third-party provider or telemetry off); when auto is unavailable (unsupported model, disableAutoMode, server-side off) the session starts in Manual (default). Corrects profile default_mode.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: On Linux and macOS Claude Code refuses --dangerously-skip-permissions when run as root or under sudo ('cannot be used with root/sudo privileges for security reasons'); the check is skipped inside a 'recognized sandbox' (mechanism not documented; IS_SANDBOX does not appear in the env-var reference or CHANGELOG as of 2026-10-15). The dev container runs Claude Code as a non-root user.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: CHANGELOG 2.1.126: --dangerously-skip-permissions now bypasses prompts for writes to .claude/, .git/, .vscode/, shell config files and other previously protected paths (catastrophic removals still prompt).
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: Corrected by B1 (2026-10-15): the built-in starting mode is auto (classifier-approved, no user prompt) for interactive sessions on >=2.1.283, and auto for -p on >=2.1.285 when feature flags are not fetched, so the rubric's score-2 criterion 'default mode asks before shell commands' is not met literally. Score-3 controls still exist: deny rules apply in every mode, bypass/auto cannot be set from project files, and disableBypassPermissionsMode/disableAutoMode can be managed. Manual mode (asks before Bash/edits) is one setting away. Reviewer to confirm whether a classifier-gated default counts as 'asking'.

facts.claim: Bash sandbox is off by default (sandbox.enabled=false); uses Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap+socat on Linux/WSL2; if the sandbox cannot start Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Linux sandbox dependencies: bubblewrap (filesystem isolation) and socat (network relay to proxy); optional seccomp filter (Unix-socket blocking) from npm @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime; Ubuntu 24.04+ needs an AppArmor profile for bwrap user namespaces; in unprivileged containers bwrap cannot mount /proc unless sandbox.enableWeakerNestedSandbox=true; sandbox.bwrapPath/socatPath managed settings (2.1.133).
facts.label: from-official-docs

D02.rationale: Seatbelt/bubblewrap sandbox exists and is centrally enforceable, but is off by default and fails open unless failIfUnavailable is set.

facts.claim: Sandboxed commands have no direct network route; traffic goes through a local proxy checking sandbox.network.allowedDomains (default empty); managed allowManagedDomainsOnly can lock the list.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Bash sandbox is off by default (sandbox.enabled=false); uses Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap+socat on Linux/WSL2; if the sandbox cannot start Claude Code runs commands unsandboxed unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true.

D03.rationale: Sandbox proxy enforces domain allowlists (default empty) and can be managed-locked; however the sandbox itself is off by default and WebFetch/MCP traffic follows permission prompts.

facts.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC (any non-empty value, including 0/false) disables auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting, /feedback, release notes, PR status badges, availability checks and feature-flag fetching; it does not cover official plugin marketplace auto-install (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL) or the WebFetch check. DISABLE_TELEMETRY and DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING also treat 0/false as opt-out; DO_NOT_TRACK is a standard boolean.
